title: Throughput Commitment Playbook & Autoscaler Interop Requirements
creator: Priya Shah
description: Purpose: Create an operationally-actionable playbook for Dedicated throughput commitments that: 1) defines measurable SLA/SLOs and error-budget accounting, 2) specifies contract language for entitlements & credits, and 3) codifies how Redwood autoscaling, burst pools, and fleet controls interoperate with contractual guarantees. Scope: dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity) for customers on monthly/annual commitments. Out of scope: hosted multi-tenant increments and marketplace third-party nodes. Key definitions proposed: - Commitment: Guaranteed sustained throughput expressed as tokens-per-minute (TPM) or requests-per-second (RPS) measured at the Redwood edge gateway after ingress shaping. Customers can elect TPM or RPS at purchase. - Measurement window: 1-hour rolling windows sampled every 5 minutes; availability is computed per window. - SLO target: 99.5% of 1-hour windows in a rolling 30-day window must meet >= 100% of committed throughput (configurable for enterprise). - Error budget: The complement of the SLO (e.g., 0.5% of hourly windows per 30-day rolling period). Error-budget burn is computed by shortfall proportion: shortfall = max(0, committed - observed) / committed. Crediting and remediation: - Credit formula: For each violating hourly window, customer_credit_hours = shortfall * committed_capacity_hours; monetary_credit = min(cap, shortfall_percent * monthly_commitment_value). Cap and floor: credits capped at 20% monthly invoice and floored at $50. - Graceful degradation allowances: Planned maintenance windows that were notified per contract (>72h notice) are excluded from error-budget and crediting if present in the maintenance calendar. - Notice & cure timeline: On breach detection, Redwood notifies customer within 60 minutes with initial diagnostics and mitigations. If breach persists for >4 hours, automatic remediation workflow escalates to on-call SRE and customer success for potential temporary capacity reallocation. Autoscaler & fleet interop: - Autoscaler behavior when a commitment exists: Dedicated pools maintain a reserved baseline equal to committed capacity. Autoscaler may provision burst nodes from a reserved burst pool for short-term surges; burst usage is billable at a premium and does not count toward the guaranteed capacity for SLO calculations. - Scaling triggers: proactive scale-up when the 5-minute moving average utilization exceeds 85% of committed capacity for 3 consecutive samples; reactive scale attempts target <2 minute median spin-up for warm nodes. - Preemption and AZ failover: If capacity is lost (node preemption/infra incident), fallback routing to compatible model variants in other AZs or regions is attempted. If failover reduces sustained throughput below commitment, that time is charged to error-budget unless failover was due to a force-majeure clause. - Fleet controls: explicit prioritization for customers with overlapping surge demands is applied using priority bands tied to contract tier. The playbook will define proportional allocation heuristics. Measurement & observability requirements: - Primary metrics: committed_tpm_config, observed_tpm_per_window, window_violation_flag, rolling_30d_violation_rate, burst_usage_minutes, maintenance_exclusion_flag. - Dashboards: per-customer SLA dashboard (token-level), rolling-window view, and incident drilldown link. - Audit logs: all scale events, routing fallbacks, and manual overrides must be stored for 90 days. Contract language deliverables: - A concise SLA clause template (summary language) and a full legal annex with definitions, measurement methodology, credit formula, caps, maintenance exceptions, and notice/cure procedures. - Customer-facing SLO table for quotes (example: 500k TPM -> 99.5% SLO -> credit cap 10%). Engineering work required: - ENG-8912: Instrument per-customer throughput measurement at the edge (owner: Dmitri Ivanov). - ENG-8940: Implement burst pool accounting and tagging (owner: Mei Chen). - ENG-8958: Autoscaler policy flags to differentiate committed baseline vs best-effort scaling (owner: Jordan Price). Acceptance criteria: - Public contract template ready and reviewed by Legal and Sales. - Production dashboards with synthetic tests showing correct detection of violations and credit computations. - End-to-end e2e simulation demonstrating scale-up within the SLA timeline (<=4 minutes for sustained ramp). Risks and trade-offs: - Conservative SLOs (high targets) increase reserved cost and reduce overall utilization; must balance with premium pricing. - Measurement at edge vs internal routing: measuring at the gateway is simpler but can under-count client-perceived throughput in rare multi-hop setups. Next steps: - Review with Legal (Marta Lopez) for credit caps and force majeure wording. - Schedule a tech-review with Serving Runtime leads to validate measurement feasibility. - Produce a customer-facing FAQ and an internal runbook for SREs. Artifacts: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/sla-playbook (draft), GH prototyping PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proto/pull/312 (burst accounting), Dashboard mock: https://datadog.redwood.ai/dashboards/SLADemo (mock).
